description: The Ruby AI framework: chats, tools, agents, MCP, structured output, evaluations, images, video, audio, OCR, embeddings, reranking, and Rails integration behind one API across every major provider.
rules: Use RubyLLM 2.x. Check the installed version in Gemfile.lock or with RubyLLM::VERSION before choosing an API. A 1.x application uses the 1.x docs at https://rubyllm.com/v1/.
Set instructions with chat.with_instructions or the Agent instructions macro. There is no system_prompt.
Limit output with with_max_output_tokens, not max_tokens.
Control reasoning with with_thinking, not reasoning options. with_thinking, with_caching, with_compaction, and with_citations take nothing or true to enable and false to disable; they reject nil.
Every with_x method on a chat returns the chat, so calls chain: RubyLLM.chat.with_instructions(...).with_tools(...).ask(...).
Pass provider: as a keyword, as in RubyLLM.chat(model: ..., provider: :anthropic). Reserve provider_options for a request field only one provider has.
Check model capabilities with model.supports?(:vision). There are no supports_vision? style predicates.
Never invent model IDs. Verify one with RubyLLM.models.find(id) before using it.
Read structured output with message.parsed after with_schema. message.content stays text.
Read tokens through message.tokens.input, .output, .cache_read, .cache_write, and .thinking, and cost through message.cost.total. An unknown cost is nil, not zero.
RubyLLM enumerations are Symbols, such as finish_reason == :stop and thinking effort :medium. Model IDs and provider slugs are Strings.
Use RubyLLM.paint, animate, speak, transcribe, ocr, moderate, embed, and rerank directly without a chat. Save generated files with result.save(path).
Subclass RubyLLM::Tool for tools and RubyLLM::Agent for reusable assistants. Connect MCP servers by subclassing RubyLLM::MCP; do not add another MCP client gem.
In Rails, run bin/rails generate ruby_llm:install and declare acts_as_chat and acts_as_message on your own models. Persisted chats use the same API as RubyLLM.chat.
